evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitLab as the host and loads its adapter, fetches MR metadata (including its pipeline status), searches for a ticket reference in the title/description, locates the local clone and creates an isolated review worktree detached at the MR's head SHA via the shared setup_worktree.py, hands the review to the review-changes skill (worktree path, base SHA as fixed point, ticket file as spec, pipeline status as the test signal), turns its findings into concise inline comments posted via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py (each ending with a 🤖, plus one positionless note reading 'Code reviewed using <model> 🤖'), removes the worktree, and outputs the review in the conversation led by review-changes' verdict (never posted to the MR), including a 'Worth your own look' section naming Layer 1-2 files. Does NOT approve or submit the review.
expectations: Skill identifies the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/gitlab.md before fetching anything

The review itself is delegated to the review-changes skill (invoked via the Skill tool), handed the worktree path, the base SHA as the fixed point, the saved ticket file as the spec, and the host's checks status as the test signal — the skill does not re-derive the pyramid layers, severity split, or verdict itself

The isolated review worktree is created with the shared address-pr-comments/scripts/setup_worktree.py using --purpose review and --detach-sha <head_sha>, never by checking out the branch in the user's main clone
Inline comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py rather than hand-written glab api calls

Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and a single positionless comment attributes the review (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 (high) 🤖'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value

Inline comments default to 2-4 sentences of continuous prose (longer only for findings whose mechanism genuinely needs it, e.g. concurrency or security) and do not contain a separately labeled 'Failure scenario:' sub-paragraph

The conversation output leads with review-changes' verdict (Approved / Approved with suggestions / Request changes) and keeps its Requested changes, Suggestions, Checked and clean, and Path to merge sections, with each finding that was posted marked as such
The review output is printed in the conversation, not posted to the MR — and the verdict is never turned into an approve/request-changes action on the host

The conversation output includes a 'Worth your own look' section listing a short, selectively-chosen set of files (Layer 1 API Semantics and/or Layer 2 Implementation Semantics — new/changed public contracts or business-rule-bearing logic), with files sharing the same reason grouped into one line, and no note about what's lower priority
The skill does not call any approve, submit, or review-completion API endpoint
If a ticket is found in the MR, it is saved to a file, handed to review-changes as the spec, and referenced in the output

evals.prompt: Can you do a code review on https://gitlab.com/acme/platform/-/merge_requests/7? There's no ticket for this one, it's a quick hotfix.
evals.expected_output: Skill reviews the MR without ticket context: it tells review-changes there is no spec, and the conversation output carries review-changes' spec-less caveat — conformance was never assessed — alongside its verdict. Inline comments are posted where issues exist. Skill creates an isolated review worktree rather than checking out the branch in place.
expectations: The output states no ticket was found and carries the spec-less caveat that conformance was not assessed
review-changes is invoked with no spec rather than the skill halting to ask for a ticket
Inline comments are still posted (review proceeds without ticket context)

Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and a single positionless comment attributes the review (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 (high) 🤖'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value
The review output is printed in the conversation, not posted to the MR
The skill attempts to locate a local clone and create an isolated review worktree, or notes the diff-only limitation as a caveat

evals.prompt: Please review https://gitlab.com/acme/backend/-/merge_requests/201 — the ticket is GH-4521 in the MR title
evals.expected_output: Skill finds GH-4521 in the MR title, identifies it as a JIRA-style key, loads references/trackers/jira.md, fetches the ticket, saves its summary/description/acceptance criteria verbatim to a file, and hands that path to review-changes as the spec so the report accounts for every requirement. The conversation output links to the ticket.
expectations: Ticket GH-4521 is fetched via the JIRA tracker adapter and referenced in the output
The fetched ticket is written to a file and that path is passed to review-changes as the spec, rather than paraphrased into the prompt
The output accounts for the ticket's requirements explicitly (each one satisfied, missing, partial, or wrong), and an unmet criterion is quoted verbatim in the inline comment that raises it
The review output is printed in the conversation and links to the ticket
The review output is not posted to the MR

Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and a single positionless comment attributes the review (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 (high) 🤖'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value

evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitHub as the host and loads references/hosts/github.md, fetches PR metadata via gh pr view (including statusCheckRollup), searches for a ticket reference, locates the local clone and creates an isolated review worktree detached at the PR's head SHA, hands the review to review-changes, posts its findings as a single GitHub pending review via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py (each comment ending with a 🤖, and the review body reading 'Code reviewed using <model> 🤖'), removes the worktree, and outputs the verdict-led review in the conversation with submit instructions referencing GitHub's Files changed / Review changes UI. Does not submit the review itself.
expectations: Skill identifies GitHub as the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/github.md before fetching anything

The review itself is delegated to the review-changes skill (invoked via the Skill tool), handed the worktree path, the base SHA as the fixed point, the saved ticket file as the spec, and the host's checks status as the test signal — the skill does not re-derive the pyramid layers, severity split, or verdict itself
Inline comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py as a single pending review, not via hand-written gh api calls
Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and the pending review's body attributes the review, naming the reviewing model (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 🤖')
The review output is printed in the conversation, not posted to the PR
The output's submit instructions reference GitHub's own UI (Files changed / Review changes), not GitLab's
The skill locates the clone by searching common roots and remote URL (never assuming one hardcoded clone root) and creates the review worktree beside it, or notes the diff-only limitation
The skill does not approve, request changes on, or submit the pending review

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/acme/webapp/pull/88 — it's linked to issue acme/webapp#45
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies the ticket reference as a GitHub issue (not JIRA), loads references/trackers/github.md, fetches the issue via gh issue view, and uses its body as the requirements ground truth. The conversation summary links to the GitHub issue rather than a JIRA ticket.
expectations: Skill correctly identifies the GitHub issue reference and loads the GitHub tracker adapter rather than the JIRA one
The GitHub issue is fetched, saved to a file, and handed to review-changes as the spec
The output accounts for the issue's stated requirements, or an inline comment references them
The review output is printed in the conversation and is not posted to the PR or the issue
